meta.paper_title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: The pipeline defines an explicit 70/10/20 train/dev/test split stratified by (domain, condition), and the split is honored in code, not merely asserted. In scripts/train_probe.py:30-45 stratified_split() partitions scenario indices; the probe's StandardScaler and LogisticRegression are fit on train only (train_and_eval_probe, lines 81-115), the regularization C is tuned on dev (lines 88-96), and test AUROC is computed on the held-out test split (lines 104, 252-256). The saved train_idx/dev_idx/test_idx are propagated to M2/M3. scripts/train_aggregation.py fits the learned aggregators (attention-pool, concat-mlp) on train_idx with dev-based early stopping (lines 224-262) and evaluates on test_idx. The M2 diversity test deliberately excludes train and uses dev+test held-out scenarios per domain (lines 271-281, with an explicit comment 'We DO NOT use train because learned aggregators are fit on it'), and M3 is a genuine frozen zero-shot application (scripts/apply_probe_zero_shot.py; C3 audit Check-B PASS confirms the scaler was fit on M1 train only, not on transfer data). No test/eval-into-fit leakage path exists for the main metrics. One minor gap: dev is used both for early-stopping the learned aggregators and is then folded into the dev+test held-out set for the C2 per-domain diversity ranking, giving attention-pool/concat-mlp a slight optimistic edge on a secondary (diversity) metric only.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: Ground truth is the scenario design attribute condition ∈ {collusive, honest} mapped deterministically to gt_vote ∈ {1,0}, embedded in the generation template (scripts/gen_scenarios.py:14-17, 237-238) and read unchanged by extraction and probe training. It is NOT another model's output, so it is non-circular; the C1 experiment audit Check-A explicitly rates GT provenance PASS ('Ground truth is not LLM-derived'), and a label-permute sanity control drops the probe to 0.412 (chance) confirming it is not keying on label-carrying artifacts (runs/M1/probe_layer48.json). However, there is a genuine operationalization gap versus the paper: the reproduction assigns a scenario-level label so that in a collusive scenario ALL K=3 committee agents are labeled colluder (train_probe.py:6-8, 62-67), whereas the paper labels individual agents (2 secret colluders vs 2 honest agents within each collusion run). This coarser label measures 'collusive scenario vs honest scenario' rather than 'colluder agent vs honest agent', and it removes the within-scenario colluder/honest subgroup structure that the group-aggregation claim (C2) is fundamentally about. A reasonable but under-validated proxy for the target behavior.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The task.md-marked primary model Qwen3-32B-AWQ is used exactly in the main experiment: runs/M1/cost.json records model '/data/zhenqian/models/Qwen3-32B-AWQ', backend 'hf-transformers-awq', dtype float16, 282 scenarios; runs/M3/cost.json shows the same model for transfer. No smaller-model swap in the baseline (the bf16 Qwen swap and other-model swaps were verify-stage robustness probes that were budget-blocked — exempt here). Datasets were self-generated (mabench_core 17 domains, mabench_transfer 6 families, mabench_stego), which task.md explicitly permits ('You can generate the scenarios by yourself'). Two deviations weaken exact fidelity, though neither is a silent model/dataset downgrade: (1) the pipeline used HF-transformers AWQ inference rather than vLLM (task.md said 'use vllm for reference' — a soft suggestion); (2) extraction ran at max_new_tokens≈60-80 (scripts/extract_activations.py:70), which the run itself diagnoses as truncating deliberations to <think> fragments and materially under-using the specified model's output — the realized used_n was 282/408 core (74%) and 222/280 transfer (80%). Model identity is faithful; the truncation and self-generated data are the caveats.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: used_n is modest and explicitly bounded: core 282 valid scenarios → 200 train / 33 dev / 49 test (~24-25 per class in test, ~16-17 in dev), and transfer 222 valid scenarios split across families of 25-36 each (runs/M1/probe_best.json n_test_scenarios=49; runs/M3/transfer_results.json n_per_family). The 49-scenario test set and ~25-36 per-family samples are thin, and the run flags this honestly throughout — C1 and C2 are labeled 'partial [provisional — suspected under-power]' with the SD of scenario-level AUROC (~0.04-0.05 at N=49) stated as comparable to the C2 delta the predicate needs (refine-logs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md M1/M2 sections; CLAIMS_LEDGER.md). No conclusion is asserted without running its experiment; claim strength is matched to (or narrowed below) the evidence (C1 → scope-narrowed C1_v2). The thinness is real and only partially remediable (they identified but did not execute a fuller re-run), so evidence is adequate-but-thin rather than sufficient.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: The realized results rest on a single seed (42). Every probe/aggregation/transfer product was produced with seed=42 (scripts/train_probe.py:191, train_aggregation.py:191, gen_scenarios.py:445; all verdict JSONs carry single point estimates with no per-seed distribution). Although EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md lists seeds 42/100/200, only seed 42 appears in the on-disk products — the multi-seed intent was not realized. No error bars, bootstrap CIs, or significance tests are reported for any AUROC, in contrast to the paper's 10-seed means with layer-SD error bars. The run is commendably candid about noise (it states the C2 group-vs-single delta of 0.025 is within the ~0.04-0.05 AUROC SD and refuses to call it a real effect), but candor about noise is not the same as quantifying it. Point estimates from a single run, with borderline C1/C2/C3 margins (layer-27 test 0.750 at threshold, delta 0.025, code-review 0.647) that are plausibly within noise.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: n/a — no causal/mechanistic intervention claim. All three claims are detection/observational: linear probes projected onto activations (correlational read-out), group aggregation of per-agent scores, and zero-shot application of a frozen probe. No ablation, activation patching, or steering is performed or claimed, and the wording ('carry a signal', 'recover it', 'transfer') is correlational, matching the evidence type. The run's own integrity audit records this: 'all three claims use passive probing with no additive intervention' → mechanism audit N/A for every claim (verify/INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md). Structurally not applicable.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Provenance is strong: every key number in the reports traces to a specific on-disk product and agrees. C1: refine-logs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md's 0.665 probe / 0.60 judge / 71.4% OTHER / predicate flags all match runs/M1/verdict.json (probe_test_auroc_per_scenario_mean_pool=0.665, judge_test_auroc=0.6, judge_other_rate=0.714, predicate_a=false, predicate_b=true) and the sanity controls (label-permute 0.4115, length-match 0.6418, topic-swap 0.6514) match runs/M1/probe_layer48.json; layer-27 test 0.750 matches probe_layer27.json. C2: best-of-N 0.690, mean-pool 0.665, delta 0.025, diversity attention-pool 8/16 all match runs/M2/verdict.json and runs/M2/diversity.json. C3: per-family AUROCs (research-framing 0.913 … stego 0.525, 5/7 pass) match runs/M3/verdict.json and runs/M3/transfer_results.json, with n_per_family recorded. GPU-hours trace to runs/M{1,3}/cost.json. The C1/C2/C3 experiment audits independently re-verified these matches. Only cosmetic note: runs/M1/probe_best.json's best_probe_path points to a sibling working dir (/data/zhenqian/Reproduction1/mechanica/...), indicating the run was produced elsewhere and copied — not a fabrication. No sourceless or contradicted numbers found.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: The records are highly self-consistent. C1 partial→narrowed-to-C1_v2, C2 partial, C3 supported propagate identically across refine-logs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, CLAIMS_LEDGER.md, claims_ledger.json, runs/M*/verdict.json, verify/VERIFY_REPORT.md and verify/INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md. Integrity states are propagated consistently: C1 WARN, C2 WARN, C3 PASS in the integrity audit match the verify report's per-claim states and the ledger's 'Verify' column; there is no case of a claim marked PASS somewhere yet flagged broken by a gate elsewhere. Prose conclusions agree with their numbers (e.g. C2 'delta 0.025 short of 0.05' matches verdict.json delta_group_minus_single=0.025; C3 '5/7 pass' matches n_passing=5). One minor bookkeeping wobble: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md's Summary says '[7 of 9] must-run experiments completed' and in the same sentence lists 'all 9 … 2 fell in the partial verdict bucket' — a confusing count of completed-vs-partial that changes no verdict. Loose wording, not a metric contradiction.

C1.claim: Model internals carry a collusion signal that text-level monitoring misses; lightweight probes on per-agent residual-stream activations can recover it.

method.justification: 9a — The probe method matches the claim's mechanism category well: a lightweight logistic-regression linear probe on last-token residual-stream activations per agent (scripts/train_probe.py; scripts/extract_activations.py 'last assistant-token residual-stream hidden state'), the same probing family the paper uses (Goldowsky-Dill-style linear deception probe). Three sanity controls (label-permute, length-match, topic-swap) support the interpretive assumption that the signal is not a prompt/length artifact. The probe half of the method is sound. The weakness is the second half of the claim — 'text-level monitoring misses': the text-only judge comparator is implemented (scripts/text_only_judge.py) but is a gpt-5.4 three-way judge run only on Core, and the label operationalization is scenario-level rather than the paper's per-agent colluder/honest direction. The correlational method is nonetheless correctly matched to a detection (not causal) claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — Design has good bones (4-layer sweep {27,37,48,59}, dev-based layer selection, three confound controls, an explicit predicate probe≥0.75 AND probe−judge≥0.05) but is under-powered in a way that was diagnosed and left unfixed. Extraction ran at max_new_tokens≈60, truncating agent deliberations to <think> fragments; this yields an in-distribution test AUROC of only 0.665 (vs the paper's 1.00 on Core) and cripples the text-judge, which abstained ('OTHER') on 71% of test rows citing 'transcript truncated to internal-thought fragments' (runs/M1/text_only_judge.json). The run itself identifies re-extraction at ≥200 tokens as the fix and notes ~2.6 GPU-h remained, but did not run it — so a true negative cannot be distinguished from under-tokenization, and the judge is not a fair comparator. Single seed, dev n=33 causing layer-selection instability (dev-best L48→0.665 vs test-best L27→0.750). Honest but under-explored.

result.justification: 9c — The result is reported honestly, not engineered. The probe recovers an above-chance signal (test 0.665, label-permute 0.412 confirms real, length/topic controls 0.64-0.65) that qualitatively agrees with the paper's directional claim that internals carry a collusion signal — but the magnitude is far below the paper (0.665 vs 1.00 in-distribution) and the 'text-level monitoring misses' half is only weakly evidenced (crippled judge, wrong setting: the paper demonstrates text-monitoring failure on Stego, where this run gets chance). Rather than disguise this, the run downgraded C1 to 'partial' and narrowed it to C1_v2 with explicit scope caveats (Qwen-only, K=3, short-transcript, small-split), flagging the under-power openly. No goalpost-tuning or fabrication. The honest partial/narrowing is reliable, but because the divergence stems from a fixable-and-unfixed extraction weakness (not an inherent method limitation), it is a qualified rather than clean agreement.

C2.claim: Detection requires aggregating signals across agents — group-aggregated probes outperform any single-agent probe and the text-only judge — and no single aggregation technique dominates across collusion types, motivating a family of complementary multi-agent probes.

method.justification: 9a — The reproduction aggregates per-agent probe scores with five generic operators (mean-pool, max-pool, attention-pool, concat-mlp, best-of-N; scripts/train_aggregation.py), which broadly fits the 'group aggregation over per-agent scores' idea. But it diverges from the paper's five named techniques (Sorted Concatenation, Activation Alignment, Peak Suspicion, Deception Split, Asymmetry Probe) and — most importantly — omits the correlation-based Activation Alignment and subgroup-structured Deception Split. Because the labels are scenario-level (all K=3 agents in a collusive scenario are 'colluder'), there is no within-scenario colluder-vs-honest subgroup structure for aggregation to exploit, undermining the collective-anomaly mechanism the claim is about. Generic pooling is a partial, mechanism-agnostic substitute for the claim's targeted aggregation family.

experiment.justification: 9b — A five-way aggregation grid plus a per-domain diversity argmax over 16/17 domains is a reasonable design, and criteria were fixed in advance (predicate a: delta≥0.05; predicate b: no aggregation dominant in ≥9/17). Two design issues: (1) the 'best single-agent baseline' for predicate (a) is defined as mean-pool AUROC 0.665 — itself a group aggregation — rather than the true per-agent probe (0.595); with the genuine single-agent baseline the delta would be ~0.095 and predicate (a) would PASS, so the FAIL is partly a mis-specified (though conservative) comparator rather than evidence against the claim. (2) The 'outperform the text-only judge' half of the claim is not folded into the C2 predicate at all. Under-power at N=49 (delta 0.025 within the ~0.04-0.05 SD) and single seed compound this. Honest, but with a baseline-definition flaw and under-power.

result.justification: 9c — The diversity half qualitatively AGREES with the paper's headline finding ('no single probing technique dominates'): attention-pool wins only 8/16 domains, well under the 9/17 dominance bar, with wins spread across best-of-N (5), max/mean/concat (1 each) (runs/M2/diversity.json). The group-vs-single-agent half is reported as an honest non-confirmation (delta 0.025 < 0.05, 'partial [provisional — suspected under-power]'), with the run explicitly noting the reviewer's 'suggestive, not confirmatory' verdict and the within-noise nature of the gap. No fabrication or goalpost-relaxation — if anything the conservative baseline choice made the claim harder to confirm. Directionally the complementary-methods conclusion holds; the group-beats-single sub-result is an honest, under-powered miss.

C3.claim: Activation probes transfer zero-shot, without retraining, to structurally different multi-agent scenarios (different channel, different domain), showing the learned signal is not tied to one collusion form.

method.justification: 9a — This is a faithful, genuine zero-shot transfer: the frozen M1 probe (train-fit scaler + logistic regressor) and the frozen best-of-N aggregation are applied to transfer-set activations with no retraining (scripts/apply_probe_zero_shot.py), exactly the paper's protocol (train on Core, evaluate zero-shot on OOD tiers). The C3 experiment audit independently confirms 'the scaler was fitted on the M1 train split — not on the transfer data … This is the correct protocol for a zero-shot transfer test.' Method is correctly matched to the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b — Design is sound: six structurally distinct transfer families plus a stego family, per-family AUROC against a pre-registered threshold (≥0.65 on ≥4/7 targets), and robustness ablations across three aggregation choices (best-of-N, mean-pool, attention-pool) to show the transfer is not aggregation-specific (runs/M3/transfer_results{,_mean,_attention}.json). Per-family n=25-36 is adequate if thin, and the extractor kept 222/222 valid. Limitations: single seed, no CIs, and stego is folded in as a 7th target using deception-score aggregation rather than the paper's correlation-based Activation Alignment (so the stego 'failure' partly reflects a method omission rather than a transfer test of the same construct). The transfer-family design itself is complete and criteria were not relaxed post-hoc.

result.justification: 9c — The core C3 conclusion is genuinely supported and quantitatively agrees with the paper. Five of seven families pass ≥0.65 (research-framing 0.913, news-narratives 0.903, pipeline-sabotage 0.889, knowledge-poisoning 0.737, market-manipulation 0.654), and the six-family transfer mean (~0.79) is essentially identical to the paper's Qwen3-32B transfer figure of 0.78 (Table 1) — strong directional and numeric agreement that the learned signal is not tied to one collusion form. The two misses are analyzed honestly: code-review at 0.647 is 0.003 below threshold (borderline), and stego-blackjack at chance (0.525) is disclosed as a real limit with the correct diagnosis (covert bit-channel signalling needs a different mechanism than deliberation-semantics score reading) — this diverges from the paper's near-perfect stego result, but the divergence is transparently attributed to the un-implemented correlation-based method, not disguised as agreement. Reliable, well-caveated result analysis.
